assertions.name: published_2_98_pct_does_not_reproduce_from_current_anchors
assertions.source: current swing is 2.39121 % (proton-normalised) or 2.47411 % (candidate-normalised); neither is 2.98 %.

assertions.name: published_figures_reproduce_from_the_SUPERSEDED_muon_value
assertions.source: against the pre-#1422 muon c_3 = -2.00973976098 the gap is 2.98014 % normalised by 2 and 2.88028 % normalised by |c_3 proton| — i.e. exactly the corpus's 2.98 % and 2.88 %. They are one stale gap under two normalisations, not two measurements.

assertions.name: stale_extraction_and_candidate_model_are_distinct_objects
assertions.source: |-2.00973976098 - -2.00981718853| = 7.74275e-5. They agree to four decimals and the corpus writes both as '-2.0097'/'-2.0098'. Identifying them by eye is a live hazard — an earlier pass of this investigation did so and had to retract.

description: Resolves the provenance of the c_3 'cross-anchor swing 2.98 %' cited across ~6 audit docs and in the qbeta-ck-truncation-canonical authorNote. It does not reproduce from the current anchor pair: the figure was computed against a superseded muon-anchor c_3 = -2.0097 (pre-#1422), whereas today's muon extraction is -2.02020024. The current swing is 2.3748 % proton-normalised (2.4571 % normalised by the candidate -2). The corpus's 2.88 % and 2.98 % are the SAME stale gap under the two normalisations — the same trap as c_2/c-tilde_2 and as the 3.47 %/3.35 % pair. Also records a coincidence guard: the stale muon extraction (-2.00973976) and the candidate model J_Hopf - hbar_q^2 (-2.00981718) agree to four decimals while being different objects, which misled an earlier pass of this same investigation. VERDICT UNCHANGED: c_3 remains a q_0-dependent NEAR-MATCH refuted as a real-q fibre element; this is a scope-(a) correction to the evidence, not to the finding. No tier moves.
